Acquired January 1, 2023 by Chicago-based private equity firm Akoya Capital Partners as a Home Services platform investment, Peerless has grown through ~10 bolt-on acquisitions since 2013 and now operates its residential pipeline through Home Depot's Pro-contractor channel: leads land in HD Portal, flow into Salesforce CRM, then move to ComputerEase (Deltek) for job costing and accounting.

phase1.label: Connected
phase1.headline: HD Portal → Salesforce → ComputerEase becomes a single, instrumented data path
phase1.body: Every Home Depot Pro lead lands in Salesforce as a Lead record within 10 minutes (UC1). When a quote is marked 'Save as Final' in Salesforce, a ComputerEase Job, Customer, and Budget Worksheet are created automatically — replacing Ashley's ~1.5-hour-per-job manual rekey (UC2). Signed contract PDFs (HS-105, 299A, 299B, HS-118) are pulled through MuleSoft IDP, extracted, and validated against Salesforce quote data (UC3). When validation fails, a structured comment or email is written back to HD Portal (UC4). The Quote Line Item object is the canonical source for picket-type, material, and Wisconsin-specific deposit rules — no Excel sheets.

phase2.label: Automated
phase2.headline: Triggers replace human dispatch on every step between lead and job entry
phase2.body: The Salesforce quote 'Save as Final' transition becomes the system-of-record trigger for the entire downstream chain: job creation, budget worksheet write, IDP validation, exception write-back. The deposit-paid status that Ashley currently looks up by hand in HD Portal reporting (UC5-potential) syncs back into Salesforce automatically — closing her aspirational quote: 'select the deposit paid box. If that could integrate and flow back through an API, that would work.' ComputerEase job status (in-progress, complete, paid) flows back into Salesforce (UC7-potential) so the operations team stops logging into Cameo + ComputerEase to check milestones. Subcontract / commission worksheet payload moves with the job header instead of becoming a second manual entry session (UC6-potential).

phase3.label: Agentic
phase3.headline: AgentForce reads the Salesforce data foundation Phase 1 built — and answers operational questions Ashley used to spend mornings on
phase3.body: Because Phase 1 created clean Salesforce objects (Lead, Quote, Quote Line Item, Project, Sales Order) keyed back to HD Portal F-numbers and ComputerEase job numbers, an AgentForce agent can answer: 'Which Home Depot leads converted to ComputerEase jobs in the last 90 days are forecasting margin erosion based on subcontract burn rate vs. original budget-worksheet target price?' / 'Which active quotes have IDP-flagged contract discrepancies that haven't been resolved within Peerless's response SLA?' / 'For Wisconsin jobs only, which deposits posted at less than the required 99% threshold?' Without the Phase 1 data path, AgentForce has no clean joined Salesforce object set to reason over. With it, AgentForce takes morning HD reconciliation off Ashley's plate.

## 1. Origin & History

Peerless Fence Group traces its roots to 1961, when Art White and Robert White founded Peerless Erectors in the western Chicago suburbs — a family fence contracting business that Robert's son Dean would grow into the largest independently owned fence contractor in the Midwest. From the 1960s through the 2000s, Peerless remained a single-brand regional operator known for residential and commercial fencing across Illinois.

The first phase of strategic transformation came between 2013 and 2019, when Dean White's Peerless began a self-funded regional rollup: Tru-Link Fence, Imperial Fence Company, Shogren Fence, IFFT Quality Fencing, Total Fencing, Link-n-Wood Fence Co., Woodland Fence, and The Fence Store were acquired in succession. By 2019, Peerless operated across Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, and southern Wisconsin — a fully integrated regional contractor with 60+ years of family ownership and a decade of consolidation behind it.

The second transformation came on January 1, 2023: [Akoya Capital Partners](https://akoyacapital.com), a Chicago-based middle-market private equity firm founded in 2005, acquired Peerless Fence Group as a platform investment in its Residential Home Services thesis. This marked the end of the family-ownership-only era. Akoya's stated investment range is $25M–$200M revenue middle-market companies — Peerless sits toward the lower end of that band.

The third transformation, announced [February 5, 2024](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20240205568305/en/Peerless-Fence-Group-Announces-Executive-Changes): Dean White transitioned from CEO to Executive Chairman, and Roger Greenhagel (previously VP of Material Sales at Peerless, formerly National Account Sales Manager at Barrette Outdoor Living) was appointed President — a classic PE-era professional-management transition. Founder Dean White remains actively involved as Executive Chairman; the operating role now runs through Greenhagel.

Concurrent with the Akoya acquisition, Peerless joined Elevate Fence Partners — a national fence-contractor platform that operates six regional brands across the Midwest, Southeast, Northeast, and a nationwide e-commerce channel. The relationship is described as a strategic alliance rather than a direct acquisition: Dean White partnered with Elevate to scale Peerless from a respected Midwest regional contractor into a growing national brand. Within the Elevate structure, Peerless is the Midwest anchor.

## 2. Business Model

Peerless Fence Group is a specialty residential fence contractor — aluminum, wood, vinyl, and chain-link — serving homeowners across Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, and southern Wisconsin. Six locations: St. Charles (HQ), West Chicago, Round Lake, Bloomington (all IL), Greenwood (IN), Cincinnati and Delaware (OH).

A material share of revenue flows through the Home Depot Pro-contractor channel: leads originate in Home Depot Service Center (HD Portal), flow into Salesforce CRM for quoting and contract management, then move to ComputerEase (Deltek) for job costing and accounting. Revenue estimates range from $15M to $32M annually, positioning Peerless firmly in the midmarket segment. A flagship commercial win was announced in October 2025: Peerless secured the contract to install 10,600+ linear feet of fencing at the Obama Presidential Center in Chicago — evidence of commercial capacity beyond the HD residential channel.

Two dynamics define the integration scope. First, the HD Pro channel is the highest-volume lead source and the most structurally constrained: HD Portal operates on its own API cadence (10-minute update cycle), its own lead identifier format (F-number, not a generic ID), its own contract documents (HS-105, 299A, 299B, HS-118), and its own write-back channel. Every new state expansion adds a new HD Portal footprint layer and state-specific deposit/permit rules. Second, ComputerEase (Deltek, version ~26.x) is a DOS-era ERP whose API surface only exists in the production tenant (no sandbox), is only accessible via a Deltek-managed relay URL routed through the CE Live Service Windows service, and is administered by a single super-admin (Jean Jacobs). These two facts together define the hardest architectural choices in the current engagement.

## 3. Corporate Stack — The Lattice

Peerless Fence Group's corporate structure has three layers:

**Layer 1: Operating Brand — Peerless Fence Group.** Family-founded 1961; headquartered at 220 W River Dr., St. Charles, IL 60174. Website: [peerlessfence.com](https://peerlessfence.com). LinkedIn: [peerless-fence](https://www.linkedin.com/company/peerless-fence). Ten pre-platform bolt-on acquisitions (2013–2019) now absorbed into the operating brand. Current leadership: Dean White (Executive Chairman, founder), Roger Greenhagel (President, appointed 2024-02-05).

**Layer 2: Operating Platform — Elevate Fence Partners.** National fence-contractor platform with a regional-brand strategy. Six sibling brands by region: Midwest (Peerless Fence Group), Southeast Florida (Florida State Fence, Foremost Fence), Southeast Georgia (Allied Fence Co.), Northeast (Jan Fence), and Digital/Direct-to-Consumer nationwide (MyFence2Go). LinkedIn: [elevate-fence-partners](https://www.linkedin.com/company/elevate-fence-partners). Platform shape: platform-above; Peerless joined via a strategic alliance.

Investment range: $25M–$200M revenue middle-market. Sector focus includes Consumer Foods & Home Services. Akoya's stated thesis: acquire a 'Platform Investment in Residential Home Services' — implying continued funding of bolt-on acquisitions in the category. Relationship between Akoya and Elevate is not fully resolved from public sources (see Signals to Watch).

## 3a. Sibling Brands — Portfolio Map

All five non-current Elevate siblings are Tier-B (lite research pass — integration signal only). Four of five are installer-contractor brands running the same HD Portal → CRM → ComputerEase model as Peerless, making each a near-identical template-deployment candidate for UC1–UC4.

Footprint: Tampa (FL), Ocala (FL). No public IT leader identified yet — capture at sibling intake. Integration signal: unknown — no public integration footprint captured. Florida deposit/permit/contract rules differ materially from the IL/WI rules already encoded in UC3's validation engine (Wisconsin 99% deposit exception will need a Florida-specific equivalent). Future-engagement note: First logical second-engagement candidate post-Peerless. Wait for Florida State Fence to express manual HD reconciliation or CE job entry pain — the pattern is identical to Peerless's current pain. NJ's regulatory complexity adds integration scope but also increases the value of the rule engine — more rules = more value of the template.

**MyFence2Go — Digital / Direct-to-Consumer (Nationwide)**
Footprint: Nationwide e-commerce material supply. Integration signal: distinct system shape — e-commerce storefront + WMS / fulfillment + ComputerEase as inventory/financial backend. Does NOT consume HD Portal Pro leads (no installer-contractor flow). The Peerless integration template applies partially: the Salesforce ↔ ComputerEase backbone is reusable; the HD Portal layer is not applicable. Lowest priority among Elevate siblings for template reuse; requires separate scoping.

**Portfolio synthesis:** Out of 5 non-current Elevate siblings, 4 (Florida State Fence, Foremost Fence, Allied Fence Co., Jan Fence) are installer-contractor brands operating the same HD Portal → CRM → ComputerEase model as Peerless. Each is a near-identical template-deployment candidate for UC1–UC4. Differences are state-specific deposit/permit rules in UC3's validation engine, a separate ComputerEase company code, and potentially a separate HD Portal tenant. The Peerless engagement designs the template; the four sibling deployments are the payoff.

## 6. Strategic Position — Why Now

This engagement is not a standalone Peerless integration project. It is a portfolio-template decision being made inside Peerless Fence Group but governed by Elevate Fence Partners' Director of IT — Brian Cook, who is already in the scoping room.

The portfolio-template angle is the primary urgency multiplier, and it is unusually concrete: Brian Cook appeared in all four scoping calls. Every architecture decision being made in these sessions will govern all six Elevate company codes.

The sibling-expansion math is equally concrete: four Elevate installer-contractor siblings (Florida State Fence, Foremost Fence, Allied Fence Co., Jan Fence) run the same HD Portal → CRM → ComputerEase model as Peerless. Each adds a ComputerEase company code and a set of state-specific rule extensions to UC3's validation engine. The template DataSkate builds for Peerless company code 00 is the template that deploys four more times — at marginal cost, not full scoping cost, if the architecture is designed for it from the start.
